researcher_profile.role: European climate and clean-energy policy analyst
focus: extreme heat and climate adaptation in Europe

record.title: Short-term NO2 exposure and emergency admissions in Greater Paris

sources.text: Using hospital and monitor data for Greater Paris 2015-2022, the study finds that short-term NO2 spikes are associated with higher respiratory emergency admissions, with the strongest effect on older adults during summer heat episodes.
The authors use a case-crossover design with city monitoring stations and report adjusted relative risks for NO2 lagged 0-2 days.
Supplementary tables list R package versions used for plotting maps.

record.title: Distributed solar PV and evening peak residual load on a French DSO feeder

sources.text: Feeder-level measurements show that higher rooftop PV penetration lowers midday net load but can sharpen the evening residual peak unless paired with storage or demand flexibility.
The study simulates 2025-2030 PV uptake scenarios on an anonymized French DSO feeder using measured irradiance and smart-meter aggregates.

record.title: A multilingual instruction-tuning benchmark for transformer language models

sources.text: The paper introduces a 12-task multilingual instruction-tuning benchmark and reports that denser models outperform mixture-of-experts baselines on reasoning prompts.
Evaluation covers zero-shot and few-shot settings across English, French, German, and Spanish with automatic metrics only.

record.title: Heatwave mortality inequalities across European NUTS2 regions

sources.text: Across European NUTS2 regions, heatwave days are linked to excess all-cause mortality, with larger relative increases in regions that combine high elderly shares and limited green-space access.
The authors argue that adaptation spending should prioritize cooling centers and urban greening in the highest-risk southern and eastern regions.

record.title: Proof-of-work mining profitability under volatile electricity tariffs

sources.text: The paper models ASIC mining cash flows under day-ahead electricity prices and concludes that profitability is dominated by hashprice swings rather than renewable curtailment events.
Scenarios assume a Texas ERCOT retail tariff and ignore European grid congestion or household energy poverty metrics.
